Calculate the common difference $d = u_2 - u_1$ of the arithmetic progression:
$$d = -\frac{\tan^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} - \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta}$$

Substitute $\tan^2\theta = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}$ and write over the common denominator $\cos^4\theta$:
$$d = -\frac{\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}}{\cos^2\theta} - \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta} = -\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^4\theta} - \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos^4\theta} = -\frac{\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta}{\cos^4\theta}$$

Evaluate the first term $a$ and common difference $d$ at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}$ (noting $\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$):
$$a = \frac{1}{\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)} = \frac{1}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2} = \frac{1}{\frac{3}{4}} = \frac{4}{3}$$
$$d = -\frac{1}{\cos^4\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)} = -\frac{1}{\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2} = -\frac{1}{\frac{9}{16}} = -\frac{16}{9}$$

Apply the $n$th term formula for $n = 13$:
$$u_{13} = a + (13 - 1)d = \frac{4}{3} + 12\left(-\frac{16}{9}\right) = \frac{4}{3} - \frac{4 \times 16}{3} = \frac{4 - 64}{3} = -\frac{60}{3} = -20$$
